en: to write a rough draft; to make a rough draft

examples.ko: 그는 고등학생 때부터 시를 습작해 왔어요.
examples.en: He has been writing practice poems since high school.

examples.ko: 매일 밤 소설을 습작하면서 작가를 꿈꿨어요.
examples.en: Every night I practiced writing novels and dreamed of being an author.

examples.ko: 습작하는 동안 선생님께 여러 번 조언을 들었어요.
examples.en: While I was writing practice pieces, I got advice from my teacher many times.
It's fine to make mistakes when you're doing practice drawings.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 희곡을 습작해 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to try writing a practice play with a friend.
I'm attached to it because it's a piece I practiced on for a long time.

explain: '시를 습작하다', '소설을 습작하다'처럼 글이나 그림을 목적어로 해서 써요. '연습하다'와 달리 창작에만 써서 대화에서는 드물고 글에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I showed the novel I wrote as practice to a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 쓴 작품을 꾸미는 형태로, 연습으로 만든 것을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, referring to something made as practice.

phrases.en: While practicing writing poems, I polished my sentences.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연습하는 동안 다른 일도 함께 했다는 뜻으로 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking form for doing something else while practicing.

phrases.en: I tried writing a poem as practice for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 시도해 본 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a first-time try.

explain_en: It takes writing or drawing as its object, as in '시를 습작하다' or '소설을 습작하다'. Unlike '연습하다', it is limited to creative work, so it is rare in conversation and more common in writing.

examples.ko: 그는 대학생 때 신춘문예에 당선돼 작가가 됐어요.
examples.en: He won the Sinchun Munye contest as a college student and became a writer.

examples.ko: 올해도 신춘문예에 시를 응모해 볼 생각이에요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of submitting a poem to the Sinchun Munye again this year.

examples.ko: 신춘문예 당선 소식을 듣고 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried when I heard the news that I had won the Sinchun Munye.

examples.ko: 신춘문예 발표는 보통 새해 첫날 신문에 나와요.
examples.en: The Sinchun Munye results usually appear in the newspaper on New Year's Day.

examples.ko: 신춘문예를 준비하느라 겨울 내내 글만 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote all through the winter preparing for the Sinchun Munye.

examples.ko: 신춘문예 출신 작가들의 소설집을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a short-story collection by writers who debuted through the Sinchun Munye.

explain: 신문사가 새해를 맞아 시, 소설, 평론 등의 작품을 공모하는 대회로, 작가가 되는 길 중 하나예요. '신춘문예에 응모하다, 신춘문예에 당선되다'처럼 써요. 작가로 처음 인정받는 것을 '등단'이라고 해서 '신춘문예로 등단하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I read the Sinchun Munye winning piece in the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에서 뽑힌 작품을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the work selected in the contest.

phrases.en: He debuted as a writer through the Sinchun Munye.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신춘문예를 통해 작가가 되는 것을 한 문장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says in one phrase that someone became a writer through the contest.

phrases.en: That writer came up through the Sinchun Munye.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 길로 작가가 되었는지 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce how a writer started their career.

explain_en: It is a contest run by newspapers at the start of the new year for poems, stories, criticism and more, and it is one of the routes to becoming a writer. You say '신춘문예에 응모하다' or '신춘문예에 당선되다'. Being first recognized as a writer is called '등단', so '신춘문예로 등단하다' is also common.

examples.en: The audience shouted for an encore loudly.
The singer sang one last song as an encore.
Even after the show ended, the encore applause continued.
The encore song was better than the main show.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 인기가 많아서 앙코르 상영을 해요.
examples.en: This movie is so popular that they are showing it again.
The encore stage was short but really moving.

explain: 앙코르는 공연이 끝난 뒤 관객이 더 해 달라고 요청하는 거예요. 한국에서는 '앙코르!'라고 외치거나 박수를 계속 치는 방식으로 표현해요. 공연이나 영화를 다시 하는 '앙코르 공연', '앙코르 상영'으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Because it's so popular, an encore performance is being held.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연이 끝난 뒤 다시 하는 공연을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A performance held again after the original run.

phrases.en: For the encore song, they sang an old song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본 공연이 끝난 뒤 추가로 부르는 노래예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The extra song sung after the main show.

phrases.example: 관객의 앙코르 요청에 가수가 다시 나왔어요.
phrases.en: At the audience's encore request, the singer came out again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관객이 더 해 달라고 부탁하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The audience asking for more.

explain_en: 앙코르 is when the audience asks for more after a performance ends. In Korea, people shout 앙코르 or keep clapping to ask for it. It is also used for repeat runs, as in 앙코르 공연 or 앙코르 상영.

examples.en: Teenagers' language habits are changing a lot.

examples.ko: 바른 언어생활을 위해 줄임말을 줄이기로 했어요.
examples.en: For proper language use, I decided to cut down on abbreviations.

examples.ko: 인터넷 때문에 우리의 언어생활이 크게 변했어요.
examples.en: The internet has greatly changed how we use language.

examples.ko: 가족과 함께 존댓말을 쓰며 건강한 언어생활을 해요.
examples.en: We use honorific speech in our family and keep healthy language habits.

examples.ko: 외국에서 살 때는 언어생활이 많이 불편했어요.
examples.en: When I lived abroad, communicating in the language was very inconvenient.
Please teach correct language habits at school.

explain: 일상에서 말과 글을 어떻게 쓰고 사는지를 크게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '바른 언어생활', '언어생활이 변하다'처럼 뉴스, 교육, 국어 수업에서 자주 보여요. 실제로 대화할 때는 '말하는 습관'이라고도 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.en: I looked back on how I used language throughout the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신의 말과 글 습관을 되돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reflecting on your own speaking and writing habits.
phrases.en_equiv: to reflect on one's language use

phrases.en: We use many loanwords in our everyday use of language.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 쓰는 말과 글 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to all the speech and writing used day to day.

phrases.example: SNS는 우리의 언어생활에 큰 영향을 줘요.
phrases.en: Social media has a big influence on how we use language.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 말과 글의 습관을 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something changes people's language habits.

explain_en: It is used to talk in broad terms about how people use spoken and written language in daily life. You see it in news, education and Korean-language classes, as in '바른 언어생활' and '언어생활이 변하다'. In real conversation, people may also put it more plainly as '말하는 습관'.

examples.en: These song lyrics are close to verse.
A novel is prose and a poem is verse.

examples.ko: 이 글은 운문으로 쓰여서 리듬이 느껴져요.
examples.en: This text is written in verse, so you can feel the rhythm.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기를 운문 형식으로 바꿔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried turning an old story into verse form.

examples.ko: 국어 시험에 운문과 산문을 구분하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The Korean exam had a question about telling verse from prose.

examples.ko: 저는 산문보다 운문이 더 읽기 편해요.
examples.en: I find verse easier to read than prose.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '산문'이에요. 시나 노랫말처럼 리듬이 있는 글을 가리켜서 국어 수업과 시험에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '시'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 시는 운문이고 소설은 산문이라서 둘은 달라요.
phrases.en: Poetry is verse and a novel is prose, so the two differ.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 '산문'과 함께 나란히 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used side by side with its counterpart, 산문.

phrases.example: 선생님이 이야기를 운문으로 써 보라고 하셨어요.
phrases.en: The teacher told us to write the story in verse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 리듬 있는 형식으로 쓴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for writing something in a rhythmic form.

phrases.example: 이 글은 운문 형식으로 되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This text is in verse form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글의 짜임이나 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a text's structure.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '산문' (prose). It refers to writing with rhythm, such as poems and lyrics, and shows up a lot in Korean classes and exams. In daily conversation people often just say '시'.

examples.en: He recites a poem in a low voice.
Grandmother did the laundry humming a song under her breath.

examples.ko: 버스 안에서 가사를 읊조리는 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was someone murmuring song lyrics on the bus.
The child softly recited a prayer and then fell asleep.
She murmured to herself as if talking alone, looking out the window.
Try speaking slowly, as if reciting a poem.

explain: 큰 소리로 외치는 게 아니라 낮은 목소리로 혼자 시나 노래, 말을 느낌 있게 입 밖에 낼 때 써요. '중얼거리다'는 불분명하게 혼자 말하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: He walked while softly humming a song to himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 부르지 않고 낮게 흥얼거릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you sing low rather than out loud.

phrases.en: She looked out the window and murmured to herself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자서 낮게 말하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking low to oneself.

phrases.en: He kept mumbling something.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 더 불분명하게 말하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but with a stronger sense of unclear, mumbled speech.

explain_en: It is not for shouting; it means saying a poem, song or words in a low voice, to yourself and with feeling. '중얼거리다' leans more toward mumbling something unclear.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 자전적 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel contains an autobiographical story.
The author published a new autobiographical essay.

examples.ko: 자전적 영화라서 감독의 어린 시절이 많이 나와요.
examples.en: It is an autobiographical film, so the director's childhood appears a lot.
It is a work with strong autobiographical elements.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 자전적 성격의 노래를 많이 써요.
examples.en: That singer writes many songs of an autobiographical nature.

examples.ko: 이번 책은 자전적 소설인데 허구도 꽤 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is an autobiographical novel, but it has quite a bit of fiction mixed in.

explain: 작가나 감독이 자기 삶에서 이야기를 가져온 작품에 써요. '자전적 소설, 자전적 영화'처럼 명사 앞에 오고, '이 소설은 자전적이에요'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 책은 작가의 어린 시절을 담은 자전적 소설이에요.
phrases.en: This book is an autobiographical novel about the author's childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작가가 자기 삶을 바탕으로 쓴 소설을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a novel based on the author's own life.

phrases.example: 감독의 가족 이야기를 그린 자전적 영화예요.
phrases.en: It's an autobiographical film about the director's family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감독의 경험에서 가져온 영화에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a film drawn from the director's own experience.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 가수의 삶이 많이 담겨서 아주 자전적이에요.
phrases.en: This song is very autobiographical because it holds a lot of the singer's life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이다'를 붙여 작품이 작가의 삶과 가깝다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -이다, used to say a work is close to its creator's life.

explain_en: It describes works in which an author or director draws on their own life. It goes before nouns, as in '자전적 소설' or '자전적 영화', and can also be used as '자전적이에요'.

examples.en: My friends critiqued each other's drawings.
The judge commented on each entry one by one.

examples.ko: 영화를 보고 나와서 장면을 품평하는 게 취미예요.
examples.en: My hobby is commenting on scenes after coming out of a movie.

examples.ko: 남의 외모를 함부로 품평하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't carelessly comment on other people's looks.
I went to a gathering where people critique the taste of coffee.

examples.ko: 선생님이 작품을 품평한 뒤 점수를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: After critiquing the works, the teacher told us the scores.

explain: '평가하다'보다 물건이나 작품의 좋고 나쁜 점을 하나하나 따져 말하는 느낌이 있어요. 음식, 그림, 영화처럼 취향이 있는 대상에 잘 쓰여요. 사람의 외모나 모습에 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The chef evaluated the taste of each dish one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식처럼 취향이 있는 대상의 좋고 나쁨을 따질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to weigh the merits of things with taste, like food.

phrases.en: Hearing the expert's critique made it easy to understand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '품평'과 함께 평가를 듣는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form is used when receiving an evaluation.

phrases.en: Please evaluate my work honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 넓게 쓰는 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but a more general, broadly used word.

explain_en: Compared with '평가하다', it feels like going through the good and bad points of a product or work one by one. It suits things of taste such as food, art and films. Using it for a person's looks can sound rude.

examples.en: Seoraksan has so many strangely shaped rocks.
A small waterfall flows down between the oddly shaped rocks.
The tourists took photos with the strange rocks in the background.
This park is famous for its magnificent rock formations.
I kept marveling at the rock formations all the way up the trail.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 기암괴석과 푸른 바다가 어우러져 있어요.
examples.en: That island combines bizarre rocks with the blue sea.

explain: 산이나 바닷가의 특이하게 생긴 큰 바위를 감탄하며 말할 때 써요. 여행 소개글이나 기행문 같은 글말 느낌이라서 친구와 말할 때는 '신기하게 생긴 바위'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: There are many oddly shaped rocks on the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구와 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase for talking with friends.

phrases.en: Strange rocks line the coast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바위가 줄지어 서 있는 풍경을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paints a scene of rocks standing in a row.

phrases.en: That mountain is famous for its strange rock formations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행지를 소개할 때 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen when introducing travel spots.
phrases.en_equiv: to be famous for strange rocks

explain_en: You use it with admiration for oddly shaped big rocks on mountains or coasts. It has a written style, like travel guides, so in casual talk people say '신기하게 생긴 바위' (a strange-looking rock).

examples.en: The hen clucked.
Every morning I wake up to the cackling of hens.

examples.ko: 알을 낳은 암탉이 꼬꼬댁 하며 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: The hen that laid an egg walks around clucking.
I can hear clucking from the yard.

examples.ko: 아이가 닭을 흉내 내며 꼬꼬댁 했어요.
examples.en: The child imitated a chicken, going cluck.

examples.ko: 닭장 안에서 꼬꼬댁 소리가 크게 났어요.
examples.en: A loud cackle came from inside the henhouse.

explain: 암탉이 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 수탉이 아침에 우는 소리는 '꼬끼오'라고 해서 서로 달라요. 그림책이나 동화에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The hen keeps clucking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 번 반복해서 암탉이 계속 우는 소리를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeated twice to show a hen clucking continuously.

phrases.en: I hear a clucking sound in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소리'를 붙여 닭이 내는 소리를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '소리' refers to the sound a hen makes.

phrases.en: The hen clucked and laid an egg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화에서 자주 나오는 장면을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A scene that often appears in children's stories.
phrases.en_equiv: to cluck and lay an egg

explain_en: It imitates the sound a hen makes. A rooster's morning crow is '꼬끼오', so the two sounds differ. You often see it in picture books and children's stories.

examples.en: It was backlit, so the face came out dark.

examples.ko: 역광에서 사진을 찍으면 분위기 있게 나와요.
examples.en: Photos taken against the light have a nice mood.

examples.ko: 해를 등지고 찍으면 역광을 피할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you shoot with the sun behind you, you can avoid backlight.

examples.ko: 역광 때문에 눈이 부셔서 앞이 안 보였어요.
examples.en: The glare was so bright I couldn't see ahead.

examples.ko: 역광으로 찍은 노을 사진이 정말 멋져요.
examples.en: The sunset photo shot against the light is really beautiful.

examples.ko: 이 카메라는 역광에도 선명하게 잘 찍혀요.
examples.en: This camera takes clear pictures even against the light.

explain: 사진이나 영상에서 빛이 찍는 대상의 뒤에서 오는 상태를 말할 때 써요. 반대로 빛이 앞에서 비치면 '순광'이라고 해요. 운전할 때 해가 정면에서 눈부실 때도 이 말을 써요.

phrases.en: Backlit photos have a soft mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 뒤에서 오는 사진을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to photos where light comes from behind the subject.

phrases.example: 역광 때문에 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: I can't see ahead well because of the glare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 정면에서 눈부실 때도 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when the sun glares from the front.

phrases.example: 친구 뒤에 해가 오게 해서 역광으로 찍었어요.
phrases.en: I put the sun behind my friend and shot it backlit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 빛이 찍는 대상의 뒤에서 오게 찍는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means deliberately shooting with light coming from behind the subject.

explain_en: Photographers use it when the light comes from behind the subject. The opposite, with light from the front, is '순광'. People also use it when the sun glares straight into your eyes while driving.

examples.en: We went to the west coast to watch the sunset.
A sunset event is held on December 31st.
This place is famous for its beautiful sunsets.
We arrived at the beach just in time for the sunset.

examples.ko: 해넘이와 해돋이를 둘 다 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to see both the sunset and the sunrise.
They say today's sunset is around five thirty.

explain: 해가 지는 일이나 그 순간을 가리키는 순우리말이고, 짝말은 '해돋이'예요. 한자어 '일몰'과 같은 뜻인데 더 부드럽게 들려요. 연말에는 '해넘이 행사'라는 말을 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Today's sunset is at six o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해넘이'와 같은 뜻의 한자어로, 시간이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word with the same meaning, often used for times and in the news.

phrases.en: On the trip I saw both the sunrise and the sunset.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대되는 짝말 '해돋이'와 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said together with its opposite, 해돋이.

phrases.en: The West Sea is famous as a sunset spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 지는 풍경이 아름다운 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for places known for beautiful sunsets.

explain_en: This native Korean word refers to the sun setting, and its counterpart is '해돋이' (sunrise). It means the same as the Sino-Korean '일몰' but sounds softer. At year's end you often hear '해넘이 행사'.

examples.en: We saw pink flamingos at the zoo.

examples.ko: 홍학은 한 발로 서서 자는 모습이 신기해요.
examples.en: It's amazing to see flamingos sleeping while standing on one leg.
A flock of flamingos was gathered at the lake.

examples.ko: 아이가 홍학 인형을 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: My child asked me to buy a flamingo doll.
They say flamingos are pink because of what they eat.
Shall we try standing on one leg like a flamingo?

explain: 분홍색 깃털에 다리가 긴 새예요. 영어에서 온 '플라밍고'라는 말도 많이 써요. 인형, 튜브, 무늬 같은 물건 이름에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: A flock of flamingos is gathered at the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 홍학은 보통 떼를 지어 사니까 '무리'와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Flamingos live in groups, so this pairing is common.

phrases.en: I bought a flamingo-shaped pool float.
phrases.nuance_ko: 홍학과 같은 뜻이지만 물건 이름이나 무늬를 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 홍학, but heard more often for product names and patterns.

phrases.en: The child fell asleep hugging a flamingo doll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 자체가 아니라 홍학 모양의 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an item shaped like a flamingo, not the bird itself.

explain_en: It is the long-legged bird with pink feathers. The loanword '플라밍고' is also widely used. It often appears in the names of items such as dolls, pool floats and patterns.

examples.en: I saw the moving moment of the victory with my own eyes.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 십 년 만에 만난 장면이 정말 감격적이었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the two met after ten years was truly moving.
The two families were reunited in an emotional moment.
I didn't know it would be this moving.
It isn't overwhelmingly moving, but it's a warm story.

examples.ko: 졸업식 노래가 너무 감격적이어서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The graduation song was so moving that I cried.

explain: '감격적인 + 명사'로 많이 쓰지만 '감격적이다', '감격적으로'처럼도 써요. '감동적'은 이야기나 영화처럼 마음을 움직이는 것에 넓게 쓰고, '감격적'은 큰 기쁨이나 고마움으로 가슴이 벅찬 순간에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 가족과 십 년 만에 감격적인 만남을 가졌어요.
phrases.en: I had a deeply moving reunion with my family after ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 만나 가슴이 벅찬 상황에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits an emotional meeting after a long time.

phrases.en: The two hugged emotionally at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사로 써서 행동이 벅찬 마음을 담고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an adverb, it shows an action carries overwhelming emotion.

phrases.en: That movie is really moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 영화처럼 넓게 마음을 움직이는 것에 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word used broadly for things that move you, like stories or films.

explain_en: It is often used as '감격적인 + noun', but it also appears as '감격적이다' and '감격적으로'. '감동적' is broad and fits anything that touches you, like a story or film, while '감격적' suits moments when you are overcome with joy or gratitude.
